Owner ruling (d), 2026-11-12: good output is the saleable board, gross minus every recorded waste line. trim_sqft + shear_sqft + reject_sqft + changeover_sqft + waste_board_sqft + admin_sqft + estimated_good_sqft = gross_sqft for the shift; each line is computed here from the reject lines and the lanes, independently of the tool.

Owner ruling (d), 2026-11-12: over September, the waste breakdown's recorded lines (trim, shear, changeover, cutoff-knife and stacker boards, dry-end, planning / admin) plus good_output_sqft add back to gross_sqft; the generator computes good output both as gross minus the month's line totals and as each setup's own good output summed, and writes only when they agree. The bale and its unexplained remainder are a scale reading, not a line.
Expected values are sums over the remaining valid setups: the 99,999,999 sq ft trim is reported in excluded_records, not averaged in.
The bad record sits in shift 2; shift 1 stays complete and unchanged.
Where the money went in shift 2: every gap priced at the post's rates; contribution reads 'margin not set', never $0.
Thursday's first shift holds the planned maintenance window (133 minutes on the v2 records): on the card, apart from the ranked losses, and in the all-in total only (the owner, PR #111).
The day of September's power outage (third shift): the outage is apart, unranked, in the all-in total only.
The same shift with paper x1.2, machine time x1.25 and a $40/MSF margin: each dollar scales with its own rate only.

The card's all-shifts total for the day: each gap summed over the three shifts and priced once on the day, with each shift's own total beside it (issue #31b review: the server's figure, not the browser's).
A question about shifts 1 and 3: the day total covers those two shifts and their 960 minutes, never shift 2.
Shift 2 holds the refused trim record: it is named in excluded_shifts and left out, and the day is priced over shifts 1 and 3 alone (their gross and 960 minutes), with the excluded record reported.
What waste genuinely costs: each bucket's MSF x paper, plus the run time shear and rejects took.
Where to look: the levers ranked by dollars a year at the post's volumes.
A $40/MSF margin and a 3% trim target: contribution is priced beside, never added, and trim points over 3% become a lever.
The golden year's last production day, all shifts: a flagged operator shift (third shift, glue / starch) and its recurrence over the year.

First shift on the day of a power outage (14 minutes on the v2 records): the outage is external (the owner, PR #111), so it is listed apart and never in the shift's maintenance, which is on target; the flag that fires is the shift's operator downtime.
A month: every one of its many flags, each with its own trailing year.
One operator flag on the v2 records (first shift, led by order changes), whose leading reason was over its band on its own once more in the year, so recurrence is not zero.
Two operator flags (shifts 1 and 3), each led by missed splices that were over the band on their own once more in the year (yesterday-review-from-tuesday asks for this day; issue #100's records).

The data's first month, January 2025 (issue #100: the records start on 1 January 2025; anchored on September 2025, the old rolling year's first month, before): the previous month is outside the records, so every previous figure is None, never zero.
The supervisor lens: the controllable losses ranked, schedule-driven trim and planned maintenance unranked.

The ownership lens: the total cost of waste, side trim first. Every line of the waste breakdown is a lever, each priced once (owner ruling (d) on PR #123): the changeover rejects, the cutoff-knife and stacker waste boards and planning / admin (not production waste) included.

lever: Dry-end: other (cracking, handling, paper, print) (all recorded)
